decisions.executionNote: Raise and gradually orient the right gripper toward the basket; keep left arm parked and preserve elbow-up continuity.
Move above the rear-left basket egg while turning the gripper downward; final alignment will use the wrist image.
Descend toward the rear-left egg with an open, nearly vertical gripper; check centering before closing.
Close around the centered rear-left egg, pause, then lift gently to visually verify retention.
Lift the retained egg clear of the basket and begin transfer toward the holder, tilting the tool inward while keeping the right wrist on its side.
Align the held egg over the holder's rear-left cup and lower cautiously; the wrist remains just right of the midline.
Lower slowly toward the rear-left cup, moving slightly forward away from the open lid; prior tracking was imperfect so replan from measured wrist pose.
The egg is no longer retained and lies on the left table. Clear the right gripper from the lid and begin a left-arm recovery approach.
Approach the dropped egg with the left arm and the remaining basket eggs with the right, rotating toward vertical grasps without crossing.
Lower each open gripper toward a separate egg: the dropped egg on the left and the front-right basket egg on the right.
Fine-center the left table egg and right front basket egg, descending only a few millimeters per step before grasping.
Correct wrist-view alignment by moving both open grippers toward the near side of their eggs, without further descent.
Correct the rejected tensor: grasp and briefly lift the left egg while centering the open right gripper over the near basket egg.
Lift and carry the visibly retained left egg toward the holder. Lower the centered right gripper slightly and close on the near basket egg.
Check right-egg retention with a slow vertical lift. The left egg slipped onto the table; reopen and approach its new position.
Carry the retained right egg above the near-right holder cup, with gradual inward tilt. Fine-center the left gripper over the loose table egg.
Both prior grasps slipped. Lower the left fingers farther around the egg before closing, while returning the open right gripper over the basket.
Replan from measured poses: slide the left jaws into better fore-aft alignment without pressing the table; lower the right gripper over the nearest basket egg.
Close the left gripper around the now-centered table egg and test with a tiny lift; continue gentle alignment of the open right gripper.
Release the unstable left contact and lift clear. Shift the right jaws forward so they surround the egg's middle rather than its near end.
Grasp the near basket egg with a gradual closure and only a small lift; keep the other arm stationary while checking retention.
Lift the right egg vertically with the same orientation and closed command; verify it separates from the remaining eggs.
Transfer the visibly retained egg above the near-right cup, keeping height and only a small inward tilt to avoid another slip.
Lower the retained egg toward the near-right cup while correcting a small rightward offset; keep the fingers closed until the egg is seated.
Make the final small lateral correction and lower the egg into the near-right cup before releasing.
Open the right gripper over the near-right cup, pause for settling, and withdraw vertically to check placement.
Clear the right gripper to inspect whether the released egg settles in its cup; align the left gripper with the loose table egg.
One egg is visibly seated in the holder. Grasp the centered left table egg more deeply, while returning the right gripper above a remaining basket egg.
Lift the left egg vertically to verify a stable grasp, and descend the open right gripper toward the rear-right basket egg.
Carry the stable left egg toward the left holder cups without changing its orientation; close the right fingers around the centered basket egg and test with a small lift.
Guide the retained left egg above the near-left cup. Reopen the right gripper and adjust its depth and fore-aft position after the failed grasp.
Fine-align and lower the left egg into the near-left cup. Move the open right jaws back from the basket rim to center the remaining right egg.
Release the left egg after a small centering correction over the near-left cup; seat the open right jaws deeper around the basket egg before closing.
Withdraw the left gripper to let the second egg settle. Recenter the right jaws on the egg after its small shift, then close without lifting yet.
Lift the third egg vertically to verify retention, and move the empty left arm clear of the holder; two eggs are visible in the front cups.
Carry the retained third egg toward the rear-right cup, maintaining height with only a small inward tilt and keeping the left arm clear.
The third egg fell back into the basket. Return above the rear egg with a vertical open gripper; avoid tilting during the next transfer.
Descend toward the rear basket egg with vertical open jaws, bringing its center between the fingers before closing.
Back the right jaws away from the basket rim and lower slowly from the measured pose; the previous approach contacted the rim rather than surrounding the egg.
Make a small forward and downward adjustment to surround the rear egg's middle with the open fingers before grasping.
Close slowly around the rear egg at the measured contact-limited pose, then make a short vertical retention test without changing orientation.
Lift the rear egg slowly clear of the basket, maintaining the grasp orientation, then start a gentle inward transfer.
The rear egg is slipping through the fingertips. Reopen above the basket and approach its middle more deeply rather than carrying an unstable pinch.
Shift the open right jaws away from the basket's left rim and center on the right of the two remaining eggs, descending in small increments.
Center the rightmost egg between the jaws with a small rightward and nearward correction, lowering only slightly to avoid the basket rim.
Seat the right fingers slightly deeper around the centered egg, then close gradually without lifting so the grasp can settle.
Lift the centered egg vertically and slowly while maintaining the closed gripper and unchanged orientation; verify separation before transfer.
Transfer the retained egg slowly toward the rear-right cup with exactly the grasp orientation preserved and the closed command maintained.
The egg slipped back into the basket. Return open and change the jaw approach angle to improve clearance and obtain a deeper grasp.
Approach the rear egg from the diagonal jaw orientation, centering it while lowering with open fingers.
Lower the diagonally aligned jaws slightly deeper around the centered egg and close gradually; the holder lid has drifted closed and will need reopening.
Test the diagonal egg grasp with a vertical lift. Prepare the left gripper for a side approach to reopen the unexpectedly closed holder lid.
Continue the left gripper's side-on approach to the lid with open vertical jaws; hold the right grasp steady while checking clearance.
Slide the left open jaws just onto the lid's left edge; move the apparently stable diagonal egg grasp closer while preserving its orientation.
Pinch the lid edge with the left gripper and test a gentle upward motion; keep the third egg stationary in the right hand.
The first lid pinch missed. Reopen and insert the left jaws slightly farther onto the lid edge, then close before testing another lift.
Test the improved lid-edge grasp by lifting and gently rotating toward the rear hinge; keep the retained egg stationary in the right gripper.
The lid did not lift. Reopen the left jaws and reposition deeper onto the front-left lip, lower and nearer to the robot, before retrying.
Pinch the more deeply inserted left jaws onto the lid lip and test a short lift. The right egg returned to the basket, so reopen that gripper.
The left fingers appear above the lid rather than on its edge. Reopen, back off slightly, and lower the side-on approach to the lid's actual height.
Try a lid-edge pinch at the lower, contact-limited height, with only a small insertion and short upward test.
Back the left fingers off the lid and lower the side approach substantially; prior pinches were above the actual lid height.
At the lower lid-edge height, insert only a few millimeters, close, and gently lift to test whether the lip is captured.
Test whether the left pinch has caught the lid by lifting along a shallow rearward opening arc; inspect for actual lid motion rather than relying on the gripper command.
The lid is visibly opening. Continue the left-hand rearward lifting arc with the pinch maintained, keeping the right hand stationary and clear.
Continue opening the lid toward upright while moving the empty right gripper away from the lid and back toward the basket.
The lid is upright again. Keep the left hand beside it while lowering the diagonal right jaws toward the rear egg for a deeper central grasp.
Fine-center the rear egg in the diagonal jaws and descend toward its broad middle rather than pinching its upper tip; keep the lid-side arm stationary.
Close around the now-centered broad part of the egg, pause, and test with a very small vertical lift while preserving the diagonal orientation.
Lift the deeper diagonal grasp clear of the basket, then begin a slow transfer with no wrist rotation and the grip kept closed.
Continue the slow, level transfer of the visibly retained egg to the rear-right cup, preserving its current grasp orientation.
